2_Introduction: The solar cells showed a drastically enhanced VOC, which led to a maximum efficiency of 23.5459% (with FF of 80.5036%, JSC of 25.746 mA/cm², and VOC of 1.136 V). The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared. The perovskite precursor solution was then spin-coated onto a substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s followed by an additional spin at 5000 rpm for 40 s. The addition of 160 µL antisolvent at last 10 s proved instrumental in achieving uniform film thickness and grain distribution. Subsequently, the samples were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—without exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators—where the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral distortion to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and halide segregation; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) ensures sufficient solute supersaturation for rapid nucleation without premature aggregation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) deposition enabling uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) shear-driven solvent extraction—synergizes with the antisolvent quenching (160 µL added at the final 10 s) to arrest intermediate solvate phases at an optimal metastable window, thereby promoting homogeneous nucleation density and suppressing pinhole formation across the film; this kinetic confinement yields large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area, as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks in XRD (no signal at ~12.6°), narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity, and uniform PL intensity mapping showing spatially homogeneous radiative recombination with suppressed non-radiative “dark spots”, collectively evidencing low trap-state density and efficient carrier extraction; the thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min further drives volatile byproduct removal and lattice relaxation without inducing cation deactivation or phase segregation, resulting in a compact, pinhole-free morphology with continuous charge transport pathways and minimized interfacial recombination at both electron- and hole-selective contacts—ultimately delivering VOC of 1.136 V, JSC of 25.746 mA/cm², FF of 80.5036%, and PCE of 23.5459%.
